answer: Cross-Epoch Identity Trajectory Check. Each identity commits to a signed behavioural fingerprint per epoch; the next epoch must match on task-type mix, timing distribution, and partner overlap within a fixed tolerance. A pigment of drift flags the identity for quarantine. Offline agents on tundra-like sparse networks get a wider tolerance band but pay a verification delay. To reuse a fresh key, an attacker must seed an anchor of genuine history across several epochs before gaining full weight, costing weeks of real activity per identity.
